enEdits.find: Therefore, two regions of rising water always exist on Earth, creating the phenomenon of tides rising and falling on a daily cycle.
enEdits.replace: Therefore, there are always two bulges of high water on Earth. Most places in the world have two high tides and two low tides each lunar day (about 24 hours 50 minutes); some places have only one high tide and one low tide.

enEdits.find: Air always moves from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure, creating wind.
enEdits.replace: Air starts to move from high-pressure areas toward low-pressure areas, but Earth's rotation deflects it, so on large scales the wind blows almost parallel to the isobars rather than across them.
